draft.title: Goods and services
card: physical things a customer can own, such as a bike, a loaf of bread or a phone.
actions done for a customer, such as a haircut, a bus trip or a lesson. The customer does not end up owning a physical thing.
Many businesses sell both. A café sells food, which is a good, and table service, which is a service.
To classify something, ask what the customer receives. If it is a thing they can keep, it is a good. If it is work done for them, it is a service.
draft.remember: A good is a thing you can own. A service is work done for you.

a.q: Which of these is a service?
opts: A plumber fixing a leaking tap
A tin of paint from a hardware store
A pair of shoes from a shoe shop
A tank of petrol from a servo
a.why: A plumber does an action for the customer, and the customer is left with no physical item to own. The other three are physical things the customer takes away and owns, so they are goods.
a.clue: Which one is work done for you, not an item you keep?

b.q: Priya runs a bakery in Bathurst. She sells pies and bread, and she also bakes wedding cakes to order and delivers them to the venue. Which describes her business?
opts: It sells goods and also provides a service
It sells only goods, because it is a bakery
It provides only services, because it takes orders
It sells only services, because it delivers
b.why: The pies, bread and cakes are physical things customers own, so they are goods. Delivering the cake is an action done for the customer, so it is a service. The business sells both, so calling it goods only is wrong.
b.clue: Look at what the customer gets, and also at what is done for them.

a.best: A plumber fixing a leaking tap

b.best: It sells goods and also provides a service
